Ruled out: a missing hedge for type-minor order, rot180 or transpose-plus-flip (adding them hurt). Also ruled out: larger footprints or other anchors, and DONE first (neither helped; differences of about 0.09 are near noise). Still open: which of the four layouts (as is, transpose, y-flip, x-flip) is the real one. Keeping only that one should remove the confusion from the three wrong components. The transposed-obs copy may help because it gives an obs frame lined up with a transposed action frame. This round: four single-layout tests built on r1c6, one 1-epoch recipe change (about 1.75x more samples), and adding y- and x-flipped obs copies to the input.
analyses.3: Round 2 found the deviation: the action layout is x-flipped relative to the obs. r2c4 (x-flip mask/output layout only, plus a transposed obs copy) scored 0.80 dev and 0.74 train. The other three single-layout nets (as-is, transpose, y-flip) scored exactly 0. So the transpose and y-flip layouts are ruled out, and so is the as-is layout, even with an obsT copy. The DONE index looks correct: the DONE-first hedge (r1c4) did not help, and 0.80 exact builds need a working stop action. Diluted hedges cost a lot: 4 layouts gave 0.37, 16 layouts gave 0. One open question: does the obsT copy matter? r1c1 scored 0.24 and r1c6 scored 0.37, which may be noise. Training success was still rising, so samples, horizon and lr are the likely bottlenecks. This round refines r2c4 with one change per candidate (no obsT, 1 PPO epoch, gamma, lr, depth), plus one combined bet.
analyses.4: The deviation is now clear: the action layout is mirrored left to right (x-flip). Nets with only that layout scored 0.80, and the as-is, transposed and y-flipped layouts each scored 0. Reading a transposed copy of the obs is unnecessary: r3c1 scored 0.805 without it and r2c4 scored 0.803 with it. The recipe matters more than capacity here. Raising lr to 3e-3 scored 0.885, the best so far, but one seed cannot separate that from the 0.80 runs. Collapses ruled out three changes: 1 PPO epoch (0.08 and 0), gamma 0.97 (0.08) and a third residual block (0.44). This is the last round, so every candidate is r3c4 with one cautious change in the direction the evidence favours: a simpler input, more frequent or finer updates, a shorter credit horizon, a wider clip range, or 3 epochs. 3 epochs is the opposite of the 1-epoch change that failed.
